observations.subject: pearl_ladder_association
observations.evidence: Association is the lowest rung of Pearl's ladder of causation: sensing regularities or patterns expressed as correlations. P(floss|toothpaste) is association only.

observations.subject: pearl_ladder_intervention
observations.evidence: Intervention is the middle rung: predict effects of deliberate actions. Mathematically P(floss|do(toothpaste)). Causality cannot be established by examining observational history alone.

observations.subject: pearl_ladder_counterfactual
observations.evidence: Counterfactuals are the highest rung: what would have happened under different circumstances for the same unit.

observations.subject: do_operator
observations.evidence: The do-operator signals experimental intervention, a mini-surgery on the model. P(Y|do(X)) is interventional, not observational P(Y|X).

observations.subject: observational_association
observations.evidence: Associations have no causal implications. One event could cause the other, the reverse could be true, or both could be caused by a third event.

observations.subject: toothpaste_purchase
observations.evidence: Shoppers who buy toothpaste are more likely to also buy dental floss. P(floss|toothpaste) is association only — no causal implication.

observations.subject: ice_cream_sales
observations.evidence: Ice cream sales and drowning rates co-occur in summer. This is a classic confounded association — summer heat is the common cause, not ice cream.

observations.subject: summer_heat
observations.evidence: Summer heat causes both more ice cream sales and more swimming (hence drowning). Temperature is the confounder Z for ice cream and drowning.

observations.subject: summer_heat
observations.evidence: Hot weather increases swimming activity and drowning risk independently of ice cream sales.

observations.subject: backdoor_adjustment
observations.evidence: Backdoor adjustment conditions on confounders to deconfound observational data. Without it, regression coefficients are not causal effects.

observations.subject: correlation
observations.evidence: Correlation does not imply causation. P(Y|X) > P(Y) is inadequate because a common cause can satisfy the condition.

observations.subject: do_calculus
observations.evidence: Pearl's do-calculus has three rules for identifying causal effects from observational data and a causal graph. It is not Bayesian network inference on associations alone.

observations.subject: bayesian_network
observations.evidence: Bayesian networks encode conditional independencies. Causal models add do-interventions and counterfactuals. LLM next-token prediction is closer to association than to do-calculus.

observations.subject: intervention_evidence
observations.evidence: Only Intervention evidence should move P(effect|do(cause)). Association evidence may update P(effect|cause) but not the interventional quantity.

concepts.name: Pearl 因果之梯
concepts.definition: Association / Intervention / Counterfactual 三级：观察相关、干预实验、反事实想象。do 算子是第二级核心。

concepts.name: 混杂与伪相关
concepts.definition: Ice cream/drowning 共变由 summer heat 混杂。backdoor adjustment 可去混杂。关联不蕴含因果。

concepts.name: do 与观察分布
concepts.definition: P(Y|do(X)) 是干预分布；P(Y|X) 是观察条件分布。LLM 语言建模更接近后者。
